summary:
- Open with a direct second‑person hook that reveals a hidden fact about the viewer’s own body or daily life.
- Keep the title under 6 words, start with “Why” or “What”, and omit emojis.
- Use present‑tense language and avoid countdown timers or on‑screen timers.
- Limit video length to 20‑30 seconds to maintain high stayed_pct.
- Focus on relatable, everyday topics rather than abstract science or niche phenomena.
winning_hooks: Your eyes are leaking right now, and your brain is hiding it.
You’re crying right now even if you don’t feel it – here’s why onions do it.
Your leg isn’t asleep because of blood loss – it’s something else.
avoid: Highly technical or distant topics (e.g., space, geology)
Hooks that don’t address the viewer directly
next_experiment: A/B test two versions of a new video on a common bodily sensation: version A uses a 5‑word “Why…” title without emojis and a second‑person present‑tense hook; version B uses a longer title with emojis and a third‑person hook. Measure stayed_pct and view growth.
